props.gloss_en: these disqualify teruma: one who eats first-degree food, and one who eats second-degree food
...and one who drinks impure liquids [disqualifies teruma]
the stam: the eighteen decreed matters are the items of 'these disqualify teruma' -- including one who immersed that day (tevul yom)
the stam: the hands are among the eighteen decreed that day -- decreed, as the Gemara reads it at 14b.5, by the disciples of Shammai and Hillel
Rabba bar bar Chana: the tanna for whom eating first- or second-degree food disqualifies [teruma] but does not render it impure is R' Yehoshua
R' Eliezer: one who eats first-degree food is first-degree
one who eats second-degree food is second-degree (R' Eliezer; R' Yehoshua says the same)
R' Eliezer: [one who eats] third-degree food is third-degree
R' Yehoshua: one who eats first-degree food [as one who eats second-degree food] is second-degree
R' Yehoshua: [one who eats] third-degree food is second-degree for sacred food and not second-degree for teruma -- in unconsecrated food prepared in the purity of teruma
the Sages decreed impurity on one who eats impure food because at times he eats impure food, takes teruma liquids, casts them into his mouth and disqualifies them
the Sages decreed impurity on one who drinks impure liquids because at times he drinks them, takes teruma food, casts it into his mouth and disqualifies it
lest you say this [eating] is common and that [drinking] is not -- [the separate listing] teaches us [that they decreed on the drinker too]
Rav Asi: at first they immersed in collected, foul cave water and poured drawn water on themselves; they began to make it keva, so [the Sages] decreed impurity on them
Abaye: keva means they would say: not these [the cave water] purify, but these and those together purify
Rava: keva means they would say: not these [the cave water] purify, but those [the drawn water] purify
the decree on a pure person on whom three log of drawn water fell: if not for this, that [decree] would not stand
Rav Mesharshiya: at first they stored teruma food beside the Torah scroll, saying 'this is holy and that is holy'; when they saw it came to ruin, the Sages decreed impurity on it
the hands [were decreed impure] because hands are busy
the baraita: even hands that come [to impurity] through a scroll disqualify teruma
[the decree on hands that come through a scroll is] because of R' Parnakh's [dictum]
R' Yochanan: one who holds a Torah scroll naked is buried naked
(entertained, rejected) 'naked' in its plain sense
R' Zeira: 'naked' means without mitzvot
rather say: naked without that mitzva
(entertained) the decree on hands in general was issued first
(inside the supposition) once that was decreed first, why would this [the scroll-hands decree] be needed?
rather, the [scroll-hands] decree was issued first, and then they decreed on all hands
tevul yom is Torah law, as it is written 'and the sun sets and he is pure' (Lev 22:7)
the verse: 'and the sun sets and he is pure' (Lev 22:7)
delete tevul yom from here [from the list of the decrees]
(entertained) the mishna's foods were made impure by liquids that came [to impurity] through a creeping thing
[foods made impure by liquids from a creeping thing] are Torah law, as it is written 'and every liquid that is drunk [in any vessel shall be impure]' (Lev 11:34)
the verse: 'and every liquid that is drunk' (Lev 11:34)
rather, [foods made impure] by liquids that came [to impurity] through hands
and it is a decree because of liquids that came through a creeping thing
(entertained) the mishna's vessels were made impure by a zav's liquids
[vessels made impure by a zav's liquids] are Torah law: 'and if the zav spits on the pure' (Lev 15:8) -- what is in the pure one's hand I have made impure for you
the verse 'and if the zav spits on the pure' (Lev 15:8), expounded: what is in the pure one's hand I have made impure for you
rather, [vessels made impure] by liquids that came through a creeping thing
and it is a decree because of a zav's liquids
Yosei ben Yoezer of Tzereida and Yosei ben Yochanan of Jerusalem decreed impurity on the land of the nations
...and on glass vessels
Shimon ben Shatach instituted the ketuba for a woman
...and decreed impurity on metal vessels
Shammai and Hillel decreed impurity on the hands
(entertained) the baraita's 'Shammai and Hillel' means Shammai and his faction and Hillel and his faction
Shmuel: eighteen matters they decreed, and in eighteen they disputed
Rav Huna: in three places Shammai and Hillel disputed, and no more
(entertained) they [Shammai and Hillel] decreed [teruma touched by hands] to be held in suspense, and their disciples decreed it to be burned
Ilfa: hands -- their decree was from the start for burning
rather: they [Shammai and Hillel] decreed and it was not accepted from them; their disciples decreed and it was accepted from them
Shmuel: Solomon instituted eruvin
Shmuel: Solomon instituted washing of hands
a bat kol went out and said: 'my son, if your heart is wise, my heart will be glad, even mine' (Prov 23:15); 'be wise, my son, and gladden my heart, that I may answer my taunters' (Prov 27:11)
Solomon came and decreed [on hands] for sacred food; they came and decreed also for teruma
the baraita: [in the eighteen] they were in agreement
Shammai: from a kav [of dough one separates] challah
Hillel: from two kav
the Sages: neither as this one's words nor as that one's; rather a kav and a half is obligated in challah
once the measures grew, they said: five quarters [of a kav] of flour are obligated in challah
R' Yosei: five [quarters] are exempt; five and more are obligated
Hillel: a full hin of drawn water disqualifies the mikveh
for a person must speak in his master's words [hence 'hin']
Shammai: nine kav [of drawn water disqualify the mikveh]
three log of drawn water disqualify the mikveh
Shammai: all women -- their time suffices
Hillel: from examination to examination, even over many days
the Sages: neither as this one nor as that one; rather a full day reduces from examination-to-examination, and examination-to-examination reduces from a full day
Hillel says to lay hands [on the offering]
Shammai says not to lay hands
one who harvests [grapes] for the press -- Shammai: [they are] made susceptible
Hillel: not made susceptible

supports.gloss_en: דתנן: רבי יהושע אומר, האוכל אוכל ראשון ואוכל שני -- שני (Steinsaltz: and a sheni disqualifies teruma without rendering it impure)
משום דרבי פרנך, דאמר רבי פרנך אמר רבי יוחנן: האוחז ספר תורה ערום נקבר ערום
דכתיב: וכי ירוק הזב בטהור -- מה שביד טהור טמאתי לך

objections.gloss_en: אמר ליה רבא: מאי נפקא מינה, הא קא טבלי בהנך? -- what difference does it make? they are immersing in those [the cave water] anyway
בלא מצות סלקא דעתך? -- could he really be buried without [any] mitzvot? (replaced by: without that mitzva)
טבול יום דאורייתא הוא, דכתיב ובא השמש וטהר! -- a Torah-law disqualification is not one of the decrees (conceded: סמי מכאן טבול יום)
וידים תלמידי שמאי והלל גזור? שמאי והלל גזור! דתניא... שמאי והלל גזרו טומאה על הידים

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא: אתו אינהו גזור ולא קבלו מינייהו, ואתו תלמידייהו גזרו וקבלו מינייהו -- both decreed; only the disciples' decree was accepted (= p_lo_kiblu)

objections.gloss_en: והאמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל: שמנה עשר דבר גזרו ובשמנה עשר נחלקו; ואילו הלל ושמאי לא נחלקו אלא בשלשה מקומות, דאמר רב הונא (p_rav_huna_shlosha) -- the eighteen were disputed, and Shammai and Hillel disputed in only three places
והאמר אילפא: ידים תחלת גזירתן לשריפה -- the hands decree was for burning from the start
ואכתי, שלמה גזר! דאמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל: בשעה שתיקן שלמה עירובין ונטילת ידים... -- the hands decree is Solomon's

answered_by.gloss_en: אתא שלמה גזר לקדשים, ואתו אינהו וגזור אף לתרומה -- Solomon's decree covered sacred food; theirs extended it to teruma (= p_shlomo_lekodashim)

objections.gloss_en: והתניא הושוו! -- the baraita says they agreed in the eighteen

answered_by.gloss_en: בו ביום נחלקו, ולמחר הושוו -- that day they disputed, and the next day they agreed

objections.gloss_en: ותו ליכא? והאיכא הלל אומר לסמוך ושמאי אומר שלא לסמוך -- a fourth dispute between them

answered_by.gloss_en: כי קאמר רב הונא, היכא דליכא פלוגתא דרבוותא בהדייהו -- Rav Huna counted only disputes in which their masters did not dispute alongside them

objections.gloss_en: והאיכא הבוצר לגת: שמאי אומר הוכשר והלל אומר לא הוכשר -- another dispute between them

answered_by.gloss_en: בר מיניה דההיא, דהתם קא שתיק ליה הלל לשמאי -- except that one, for there Hillel was silent before Shammai
